canonical_data: projects, sessions, plans, plugin registry, settings, and an audit log in a local SQLite database, with keychain-held credentials
strengths: A Rust host core evaluates a permission request for each risky tool call and records allow-once, allow-session, or deny, with audit records written in the same transaction as security-relevant state changes
Plan is a durable session state with an approval record and an atomic transition to execution, rather than a prompt convention
Sessions, worker sessions, and subagent transcripts stay inspectable, and local sessions from Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi can be imported
weaknesses: The README marks the 0.17.x line as Early Preview, and the Agent Engine is the separate pi packages, so loop behaviour depends on an external project at pinned versions
Tools execute on the host under workspace path enforcement and the permission layer; the reviewed documentation describes no operating-system sandbox
Plugins can add tools, background services, and MCP servers, which widens what a session can reach beyond the core's own review
Licensing is mixed: the root is LGPL-3.0 while a bundled file-manager plugin carries a separate MIT file
why_it_matters: A fast-moving, openly licensed desktop product that treats the coding-agent session, its permissions, and its plugins as one persistent workspace.
